title: Replace services file with static array
description:
To speed up start-up we no longer read the services file
from an external resource. Instead it is compiled statically
into the binary in a sorted array.

The personal services file is still parsed and loaded at startup,
if it exists, to allow users to add custom entries and override
global entries.

For historical reasons the port list is mostly composed of
the same entry for TCP and UDP. To avoid a lot of duplication
we add an extra TCP+UDP table and do two lookups for TCP or
UDP, one in the TCP+UDP table and the other in the TCP/UDP table.

Because the services name space is pretty sparse, with lots of
holes, we also use a binary search instead of a linear array
with aprox. 49000 entries, where most would be empty.

Does this affect the information in the WSUG [B.3. Configuration Files](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html/#ChAppFilesConfigurationSection) section on `services`?  
  
Windows ships with a `services` file in `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc` but the version shipping with Wireshark includes more entries. Seems like users might be missing out on a local reference source by not still shipping the file or maybe there should be a companion to https://www.wireshark.org/tools/oui-lookup.html for `services`.

> Does this affect the information in the WSUG [B.3. Configuration Files](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html/#ChAppFilesConfigurationSection) section on `services`?

Not if !11379 is merged.

> Windows ships with a `services` file in `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc` but the version shipping with Wireshark includes more entries. Seems like users might be missing out on a local reference source by not still shipping the file or maybe there should be a companion to https://www.wireshark.org/tools/oui-lookup.html for `services`.

If I understand what you are saying correctly shipping our services file or not has no bearing on using local reference sources (which was never the case for Windows anyway AFAIK).
Sorry - I meant "local reference" as in manually grepping or scanning through the file for a port number or service name.

Oh I see. In that case I agree users may miss out on that but it's not its purpose, to serve as a local reference, so I do not consider it an issue personally. I suppose IANA should be the reference for that (not local but :shrug: ).
What about augmenting tshark to export the previously external but now compiled in files, such as `tshark -G enterprises`?
It is a possibility but to be generally useful we would need to compile in the long form name too and that would increase the size footprint considerably.
@geraldcombs update-ws-numbers needs to commit changes to `epan/services-data.c` with this MR.
Done.
